MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 27, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:01 p.m., on August 27, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 22, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator, Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  property commonly referred to as "Casta del Sol Golf Course" located at 27601 Casta
  del Sol, Mission Viejo, California. City of Mission Viejo Negotiators: City Manager
  Dennis Wilberg, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay,
  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and City Attorney William Curley,
  III. Negotiating Party: Professional Real Estate Services (PRES) President Brad
  Schroth. Under discussion price and terms.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  1  August 27, 2019
 At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received updates and gave direction to staff
but no reportable actions occurred. He said he anticipates that staff will have some definitive
information at either the next Council meeting, or a special meeting prior to that, for presentation
to the City Council and the public.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation on Nest Box Project and Bird Habitat Value of Aurora Park

  The City Council received the presentation from student naturalist, Lara Tseng.

P2. Mission Hospital Presentation on Heart & Vascular Institute Programs

  The City Council received the presentation from Susana Robison, Director of Cardiovascular
  Services, and Erika Mamich, Nurse Manager.

P3. Featured Businesses of the Month - Enid’s Wig Salon and The Bee Man

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to Enid Seal and Jerry Bryant.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jerry Bryant, MV: Expressed his concerns about the bidding process for bee control services
within the City and stated that he was never asked to provide a proposal.

Hadia Karzai, Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee Member, M.V.: Announced that
the character word for the month of August is self-control.

Kathy Marvin, MV: Expressed concerns about the intense lighting and unbearable noise levels at
the Marguerite Aquatics Complex during very early morning hours and late into the evening.

Diana Morena, MV: Stated that she is the co-founder of Web Design Pilot which offers web design
services. She is also a member of the Chamber of Commerce and she thanked the Council for their
support.

Margie Wakeham, CEO of Families Forward, MV: Announced her upcoming retirement and
thanked the Council for their support. She introduced her successor Madelynn Hirneise.

City Council Minutes  2  August 27, 2019
 Brian Lochrie, Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA), Irvine: Provided information on the new
TCA FastTrack transponder decal which was mailed out to account holders to replace the hard
case transponders.

Madjid Niroumand, MV: Spoke about the excessive lighting and noise coming from the
Marguerite Aquatics Center and asked for the Council’s help to rectify this problem in his
neighborhood.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the Special City Council meeting of July 9, 2019, as presented,
  and (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of July 9, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated July 5, 2019 in the Amount of $1,964,382.88

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated July 12, 2019 in the Amount of $618,040.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated July 19, 2019 in the Amount of $1,019,010.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated July 26, 2019 in the Amount of $500,355.98

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated August 2, 2019 in the Amount of $1,376,082.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated August 9, 2019 in the Amount of $977,942.52

City Council Minutes  3  August 27, 2019
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Check Register Dated August 16, 2019 in the Amount of $3,438,925.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2019

  Received and filed.

10. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for June 2019

  Received and filed.

11. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for June 2019

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2019

  Received and filed.

13. Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending June 30, 2019

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending June
  30, 2019.

14. Destruction of Records - Citywide Annual Records Purge

  Adopted Resolution 19-24 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain City
  Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.

15. Alicia Parkway & Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 17232) and
  Santa Margarita Parkway & Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP
  17233)-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

City Council Minutes  4  August 27, 2019
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

16. Proposed Abatement of Weeds on Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed
  Abatement Program 2019

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Raths opened the Public Hearing 6:52 p.m. There being no public comments, Mayor
  Raths closed the Public Hearing at 6:52 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  instruct the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in
  accordance with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

17. Purchase and Installation of a Glacier Pool Cooler for the 50 Meter Pool at the
  Marguerite Aquatic Complex

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  Create CIP 20326 to install a Glacier Pool Cooler for the 50 Meter Pool at the Marguerite
  Aquatic Complex; (2) award a contract to Aquatic Design Group in an amount not to exceed
  $29,500 for the creation of working drawings for the project, and (3) adopt Resolution 19-
  25 Amending the FY 2019-20 Capital Improvement Program by Establishing a Capital
  Improvement Project and Appropriations for a Pool Cooler at The Marguerite Aquatics
  Complex.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had no report.

City Council Minutes  5  August 27, 2019
 19. Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

20. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

21. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

23. Consideration of Policy Regarding Town Hall Meetings Conducted by Individual
  Council Members

  Council Member Bucknum presented her report.

  Rhonda Reardon, MV: Stated that she feels the policy is unnecessary and she asked that the
  Council work together and be respectful of one another.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum to adopt the policy as presented. The motion
  died for lack of a second.

Council Member Bucknum asked her colleagues to consider the spirit in which her proposed policy
was offered. She said that it was her effort to make sure that the City is never accused of any
special favors to those that are sitting on the dais, over any other person seeking election. She also
wanted to make sure that staff and Police Services are given ample time to prepare and notify the
public for this type of meeting. She outlined the summer events that she attended which included
concerts in the park, Little League tournaments, a Marine Adoption Committee fundraiser, Eagle
Scout awards ceremonies, the Pacific Symphony event, and the Masters National Swimming
Championship. Council Member Bucknum stated that the City needs to look into the complaints
about the lighting and excessive noise at the Aquatics Center so that the neighbors can enjoy their
homes. She announced the City will partner with Annie Nelson of American Soldier Network for
this year’s Patriot Day Ceremony at the Norman P. Community Center. She thanked Annie for
reaching out to the City Council and staff for partnership on this and future events for veterans. In
conclusion, Council Member Bucknum wished everyone a great Labor Day weekend.

City Council Minutes  6  August 27, 2019
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley complimented staff on the Symphony in the park and stated that it is a
great opportunity for children to experience such an event. She gave a special shout-out to longtime
volunteer Ezio Petrella, President of Little League District 68, whose efforts brought the Little
League State Championship Tournaments to Mission Viejo. She noted that she was able to attend
a few of the games and had the honor of throwing out the first pitch at one of the games. Council
Member Kelley discussed her attendance at National Night Out and thanked to Khatra Molina and
Paula Monical for the great event. She also thanked Hadia Karzai for attending the meeting tonight
to speak about the character word of the month and she encouraged residents 13 years and older
to volunteer for the Community of Character Committee.

Council Member Sachs

Council Members Sachs complimented staff for the paving work that was done on Olympiad Road
and he thanked the construction company for a job well done. He announced that he had a great
lunch with Dr. Stern, the President of Saddleback College. They discussed the college’s hospitality
program and the possibility of constructing a hotel on City property adjacent to the school to be
used as a training facility for the hospitality students. Council Member Sachs suggested that
perhaps the Los Angeles Chargers could use the new Saddleback College stadium for spring
training and that they could have access to the proposed hotel. In conclusion, he expressed his
appreciation to Council Member Bucknum for what she was trying to accomplish with her agenda
report (item 23).

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell agreed with Council Member Sachs’ comments regarding the policy that
Council Member Bucknum proposed. He stated that he had a very busy summer and that the break
was nice, although there was still a lot of work going on. He announced that he competed in the
Masters National Swim Meet at the Marguerite Aquatics Center and he placed 9th in the 50-meter
backstroke. The Nadadores women’s team won the national championship and the men’s team
came in second. He also expressed his admiration for the San Diego Masters Team that is
comprised of swimmers who are 80 years-old and over, and who won all of their relays in the
event. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell apologized to the neighbors of the aquatics facility for the loud
noise and excessive lighting and said that there can be some solutions found. He also praised
Mission Hospital for their professionalism and Orange County Fire Authority for their quick
response time during a recent event with a family member. He thanked the ambulance drivers and
paramedics who helped and said he is very thankful that there are such great public safety people
serving Mission Viejo.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths thanked City staff for an amazing summer with Pacific Symphony and all the other
events that the residents enjoyed. He joked about the rumor that there are photos of him belly
flopping at the recent belly flop and cannon ball contest at Sierra Recreation Center. In closing,
Mayor Raths invited residents to attend the Rotary Club breakfasts on Wednesday mornings
beginning at 7:00 a.m. at the Mission Viejo Country Club.

City Council Minutes  7  August 27, 2019
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:56 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 10, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 10, 2019

City Council Minutes  8  August 27, 2019
